vs
Noor Jahan Begum and others ------ Plaintiff-Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
By this Rule the Opposite Party Nos. 1-5 were called upon to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 17-6-1996 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 3rd Artha Rin Adalat, Chittagong in Other Class Appeal No. 40 of 1993 allowing the appeal, decreeing the suit on setting aside those dated 31-10-1992 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Boalkhali, Chittagong in Other Class Suit No. 59 of 1990 dismissing the suit should not be set aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 4. Both the parties examined witnesses in support of their respective cases. The learned Assistant Judge upon consideration of the evidence on record came to finding that the deed of will dated 25-3-81 was duly executed and registered on commission and the plaintiffs failed to prove their case and with this observation dismissed the suit by the judgment and decree dated 31-10-1992. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and decree the plaintiffs preferred other Appeal No. 4 of 1993. 

 5. The Appeal was heard by the learned Subordinate Judge, 3rd Artha Rin Adalat, Chittagong who by the impugned judgment and decree dated 17-6-96 allowed the appeal and decreed the suit declaring deed of will dated 25-3-81 to be a void deed. 

 6. Being aggrieved by this judgment and decree the defendant has obtained the instant Rule. 

 7. Mr Enayetur Rahim, the learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioner, took me to the judgment of both the Courts below and submitted that the learned Subordinate Judge upon misconception of law and fact has decreed the suit although no evidence is available on record in support of his finding. He prayed for interference against the impugned judgment and the decree. 

 8. Mr Khurshid Alam Khan with Mr Mujibur Rahman supported the impugned judgment and decree. Mr Khurshid Alam Khan submitted that the deed in question is void in view of the fact that the deed of will 'Nirupan Patra' shows that the same was not executed wilfully by Obaidur Rahman and the Court of appeal rightly decreed the suit. 

 13. In the result, the Rule is made absolute however without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and decree dated 17-6-1996 passed by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, 3rd Artha Rin Adalat, Chittagong in Other Class Appeal No. 40 of 1993 are hereby set aside. The judgment and decree dated 31-10-1992 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Boalkhali, Chittagong in Other Class Suit No. 59 of 1990 are hereby restored. The order of stay granted by this Court dated 13-8-1996 is hereby vacated.
